speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the onset and progression of this painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg? I also need to know if you have any history of diabetes, vascular disease, or recent trauma to the area.

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the lesion's appearance after an insect bite, I suspect erythema nodosum or pyoderma gangrenosum. Do you have any associated symptoms such as joint pain, fever, or changes in your bowel habits recently?

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pitting edema and varicose veins strongly suggests a venous etiology, likely a venous stasis ulcer that was triggered by the trauma of the ant bite.
